title: Model Repository (Textable, Record)
documentation:
## Purpose
Identifies which external model repository a model spec resolves against. Currently the only supported value is `huggingface`, which causes the system to resolve model specifications against the HuggingFace Hub API and download infrastructure.

## When to use
Use this type as a parameter when a cap needs to know which registry to query. Most model specs encode the repository in their prefix (e.g. `hf:` for HuggingFace), so this type is primarily useful when the repository must be specified separately from the spec string.

## Notes
The allowed value is `huggingface`. Additional repository types may be added in future; implementations should reject unknown values rather than silently defaulting. See [Model Spec](https://capdag.com/browse/media:model-spec;textable) for the combined spec format.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Record marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is a key-value mapping at its
root: a JSON object, a CSV row with named columns, a TOML table, an INI file.
Independent of `list-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is a key-value mapping. Consumers can expect to address
fields by name.
